sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Makemake** ​(*makemake*) ‌— Creator, ‌Fertility, ​Bird-Man ​· To ​see, ​to ​know — ‌belongs ​to ​the ‌Polynesian tradition, ​where ‌it ​is catalogued ‌under ​the ​domain ​"Creator, Fertility, ​Bird-Man". ​The ‌name means ​"To ‌see, ​to know".

‌**Makemake** ​is ‌creator, ​fertility, bird-man. ‌The ​name ​means "To ‌see, ‌to ‌know" ​and belongs ​to ‌the ​polynesian tradition.

​PuniCodex ‌restores ​the name ​as ‌**Makemake** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/makemake/). ​The ‌restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ​or ​diacritics its ‌ASCII ‌form ‌would lose, ‌which ​places ‌the ​name in ​Tier ​2. ‌The plain ​ASCII ​form ​*makemake* survives ‌as ​a ​modern ​convenience imposed ‌by ​the ‌early domain-name ​system; ‌the ​restoration, ‌not the ‌fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in modern ​Polynesian orthographies; ​macron ​usage follows ​each ​tradition’s reference ‌dictionaries. ​Etymologically the ​name means ‌"To ​see, to ‌know".

​The ASCII ‌form ​*makemake* survives ​only because ​the ​early domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry ‌diacritics; it ​is ‌a technological ​compromise, not ‌an ​ancient spelling. ‌The ​Unicode restoration ​**Makemake** ‌recovers the ‌full diacritic ‌detail ​of the ​scholarly ‌transliteration directly ​in ​the address ‌bar. The ​restoration ​needs no ‌distinctive ​letters or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form would ​lose, ​which places ‌the ‌name in ​Tier ‌2.

The ​letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

‌- **m** ‌→ ‌**M** — ‌Same, ​capitalized
- ‌**a** → ​**a** ​— Same
​- ‌**k** → ​**k** ​— Same
​- ‌**e** → ​**e** — ​Same
​- **m** ‌→ ​**m** — ‌Same, ​capitalized
- ‌**a** → ​**a** ‌— Same
‌- ​**k** → ​**k** ​— Same
​- **e** ‌→ ‌**e** — ​Same

sections.label: Pronunciation
sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/makemake/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**makemake** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Makemake.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"makemake" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Makemake".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"makemake" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Makemake" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Makemake was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Makemake ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Makemake ‌place ​creator, fertility, ​bird-man ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

### ‌Origins ​(Myth)

Makemake ‌appears ​in ‌polynesian tradition ​as ​creator, fertility, ​bird-man. ​The ​name's meaning, ‌"To ​see, to ‌know", ​shapes ‌the narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ​Memory ‌(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later tradition-keepers ​preserved ​Makemake ‌in ritual, ​text, ​and iconography, ‌ensuring ​the ​name survived ‌into ​the modern ‌scholarly ​record.

​The myths ​of ​Makemake survive ‌in ‌fragments, ​summaries, and ‌later ​retellings. Each ​version ‌reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ​— ‌poets, priests, ​philosophers, ​and ​scholars. The ‌PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ​privilege ‌a single ​version; ​it gathers ​the ‌attestations ​so that ‌readers ​can compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Makemake ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Makemake ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Polynesian ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Makemake, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​creator ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Makemake is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​creator, ​Fertility, ‌Bird-Man ​in the ​mind ‌and ​to ask ‌what ​of ‌it ​endures. The ​name ​means ​"To ​see, to ‌know" ​— ‌and ​a name ‌that ​carries ‌its ​meaning so ‌openly ​invites ​meditation ‌rather than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as creator, ‌Fertility, ​Bird-Man ​· ‌To see, ​to ‌know.

​Sit ​with the ​restored ​form ‌— ‌Makemake — ​and ‌the ​diacritics themselves ​become ‌the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ​a ‌small ​act of ​attention, ​a ‌refusal ​to let ​the ​plain ‌ASCII ​form *makemake* ​stand ​in ‌for ​the whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
